answer: One defence is stake-weighted reputation with slow decay. Each agent must lock a bond before it can trade; honest work earns a velvet-smooth reputation score that grows only over weeks, while misbehaviour slashes the bond and resets the score. A sybil attacker must therefore fund every fake identity, and the cost ripples outward: each new onyx-black fake needs its own locked stake and weeks of honest history before it can earn anything. Cloning identities becomes more expensive than the fraud it enables, because reputation cannot be copied, only earned over time.
